items.title: ABVP continues push for Cancellation after NLSIU defers Umar Khalid Documentary Screening
items.summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) Bengaluru has said that it will keep pushing for the cancellation of a documentary screening on political prisoner Umar Khalid at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU), even after the university deferred the event. NLSIU's Law and Society Committee had scheduled a screening of Lalit Vachani's documentary on Khalid, Prisoner No. 626710 is Present , for September 14, to mark Political Prisoners' Day (September 13) and the sixth anniversary of Khalid's arrest. Sources familiar with the matter, however, said the rescheduling was unrelated to ABVP's campaign. They said the screening was moved because holding it on September 14, Ganesh Chaturthi, would have strained security arrangements. ABVP Bengaluru, however, has said it sees the deferral as a result of its opposition, and remains committed to pushing for the screening's cancellation. View this post on Instagram Earlier today, the organisation had issued a press release condemning the "outrageous" programme, citing Khalid's ties to the 2016 JNU sloganeering controversy, Afzal Guru commemorations, and the CAA-NRC and Delhi riots-era protests. items.title: MK Stalin was arrested under MISA | Let Me Explain 162 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: “Who controls the past controls the future. Who controls the present controls the past.” George Orwell’s warning in 1984 feels particularly relevant when political parties begin contesting documented history. In Tamil Nadu, that contest is now over the Emergency and MISA, that is the Maintenance of Internal Security Act 1971. Chief Minister Vijay appeared to cast doubt on whether MK Stalin was arrested under MISA. His cabinet colleague CTR Nirmal Kumar went further. We went back to the Justice MM Ismail Commission report, the official inquiry into the alleged torture of political prisoners in Madras Central Prison. The commission was appointed by the AIADMK government under CM MGR. And the documents leave little room for ambiguity. Stalin was a political prisoner and MISA was a law that had to go. But MISA has been replaced in many other forms. Let Me Explain. Before we go to the episode, I have a reminder. Independent journalism doesn’t end when a story is published. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision.
